substitution_evidence: Intro 1/T5: one towel → “It is a towel.”; omission of `a` and plural `towels` both fail the one-item condition.
Intro 2/T6: two curtains → “They are curtains.”; `a curtains` is the realistic extraneous-article error, while `a curtain` names one item.
Intro 3/T9/T13: several pillows → plural bare `pillows`; `a pillows` and `a pillow` respectively test extra `a` and singular transfer.
T10: one water glass → `a glass`; T15: several water glasses → bare `glasses`. These give the returned word both sides of the contrast.
T11/T16: one curtain → `a curtain`; T12: dictated plural negative retains bare `towels`; T17: one pillow → “It is a pillow.”

boundary.article_rule_scope: The source limits the contrast to its taught naming frames and explicitly avoids claiming that plurals never take articles.

traps.diagnostic_quality: Both omission of `a` for a singular and overgeneralized `a` before plurals are directly tested; the intentionally ungrammatical plural-article distractors are appropriate target errors.

reason: S21 cleanly teaches the specified indefinite singular-versus-bare-plural contrast through grounded, uniquely answerable delivery-note scenes, with adequate retrieval and independent final production.
